key_fields.sql: select z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone, count(t.pulocationid) as cash_trips from ops.zones z left join lake.trips t on t.pulocationid = z.locationid and t.payment_type = 2 group by z.locationid, z.borough, z.zone order by z.locationid
facts: lake.trips.pulocationid: 495833 rows, 495833 non-NULL, 243 distinct → NOT unique (repeated values)
lake.trips.payment_type: 495833 rows, 495833 non-NULL, 5 distinct → NOT unique (repeated values)

value.bottleneck: The query spends most of its time scanning the trips table (495k rows) to filter payment_type=2, then hash-joining the 99k matching rows to the tiny zones table (265 rows) and grouping. The sequential scan on trips is the largest data movement.

hypotheses.claim: The sequential scan on trips reads all rows to evaluate payment_type=2; creating an index on payment_type (if DuckDB supported secondary indexes) or partitioning the table by payment_type would avoid the full scan.
The join condition CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID forces a per-row cast on the 99k probe rows; aligning the data types of PULocationID and LocationID would eliminate this CPU overhead.
The hash group by processes 99k rows with string columns (Borough, Zone) in the grouping key; replacing those with integer surrogates (e.g., zone_id) would reduce hash/comparison cost.
